implementation.boundary: The existing action executor saves a pending intent and starts the bound Flow without physical CRUD. The same action/idempotency row is resumed under database locks; there is no second action or second approval request.
implementation.storage: Existing idempotency and outbox tables retain input/actor/configuration version, the full effective configuration snapshot, Flow binding/version and readable execution outcome. No Base files, schema changes or replacement framework.
implementation.recovery: The existing outbox scheduler reconciles durable terminal Flow instances. Business writes, their audit, result update and one completion outbox commit together. Failed attempts roll back before a separate transaction records CONFLICT or EXECUTION_FAILED.
implementation.authorization: The coordinator reads the stored Flow outcome, verifies its linkage, restores the original actor with current permissions, checks active account/system/tenant/member, and issues a package-restricted execution permit. Physical handlers recheck current field/data/ownership constraints and expected record version.
implementation.configuration: A changed module version or changed effective configuration, including independent overlays, blocks execution. Neither a retry nor an approval silently migrates the submitted intent.
implementation.cancellation: Rejected, withdrawn, terminated and returned Flow outcomes never execute the pending CRUD. Terminal action results stay terminal on retry.
implementation.runtime_flow: AFTER_APPROVAL reviews a record-less intent so Flow writeback/status nodes cannot prematurely mutate its effective target. Record-owner approval resolves the proposed owner or the original target owner. The Flow completion message distinguishes approval completion from business execution.
implementation.frontend: A shared receipt panel distinguishes pending, executed, rejected, withdrawn and failed/conflicted outcomes. It supports authorized refresh/retry and stores only the latest receipt id per actor/module in sessionStorage. The existing shared create/update/delete caller consumes it.
implementation.scope_reason: Approval restoration is an internal continuation of the chosen FoundationControlService boundary. FlowRuntimeService/participant resolution and shared receipt UI are direct dependencies needed to preserve business semantics.

limitations: B01.4 core contract is verified. The complete product and full Flow feature set are not certified.
The three registered approval-resume handlers are CREATE/UPDATE/DELETE. Transfer/conversion and other actions remain B07.
Legacy import, AI and application methods that promise a physical record still reject FLOW_ONLY and AFTER_APPROVAL transactionally; full receipt adaptation remains B13/B17/B11.
A data-tenant membership is still required to initiate a bound Flow; cross-tenant delegation remains B03/B11.
Effective configuration drift requires resubmission; no automatic intent migration or implicit overwrite is performed.
Flow form edits/writeback nodes do not update the frozen intent. Full approval form semantics, advanced Flow operations and action-causation propagation remain B08-B10.

The complete tenant-extension publication journey is not newly certified here. A same-version mismatch is injected into the pending intent snapshot to verify the conflict guard; published versions and their immutable protection are preserved. Normal approval cases verify faithful effective-snapshot round-tripping.

The receipt panel was built and its shared outcome logic tested, but it has not received browser visual acceptance. It restores the latest receipt per module within a browser tab; a complete action history belongs to the later workflow UI.
Shared shells/layouts are next (B02), full field runtime remains B05 and complete shared forms remain B06.
